claim_verdicts.evidence: "The reclaim policy for a PersistentVolume tells the cluster what to do with the volume after it has been released of its claim. Currently, volumes can either be Retained, Recycled, or Deleted." Field name persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy confirmed in the PersistentVolume API reference and in reclaim-policy.sh line 10. (Local mirror is the v1.37 site; section unchanged in substance for 1.34.)

"If no reclaimPolicy is specified ... it will default to Delete." Binding mode (added in round 2): "specifying the WaitForFirstConsumer mode which will delay the binding and provisioning of a PersistentVolume until a Pod using the PersistentVolumeClaim is created." kind's standard: captured output "standard (default)   rancher.io/local-path   Delete".

Round 2: lesson now says the volume "disappears from kubectl get pv, and the storage behind it is deleted with it"; the unsourced local-path folder detail is gone. Docs: "deletion removes both the PersistentVolume object from Kubernetes, as well as the associated storage asset in the external infrastructure."

"When the PersistentVolumeClaim is deleted, the PersistentVolume still exists and the volume is considered \"released\". But it is not yet available for another claim because the previous claimant's data remains on the volume. An administrator can manually reclaim the volume"

Execution (captured output at stage-3): after `kubectl delete pvc data kept`, the list shows only "kept    retain-local   Retain    Released". Phase definition: "Released: the claim has been deleted, but the associated storage resource is not yet reclaimed by the cluster".

Docs recovery procedure: "Delete the claimRef entry from PV specs, so as new PVC can bind to it. This should make the PV Available." — so a Released PV keeps claimRef and is not bound until it is removed. Retain: "not yet available for another claim". Output: CLAIM column (.spec.claimRef.name) still reads kept after the claim is deleted.

"This deletes _everything_ under the namespace!" and "low-level resources, such as Nodes and PersistentVolumes, are not in any namespace." Output: after `kubectl delete namespace storage-lessons` the list has no data line.

"automated sync will not delete resources when Argo CD detects the resource is no longer defined in Git"; pruning "can also be enabled to happen automatically as part of the automated sync" with prune: true (WebFetch summary of stable docs, not a 3.1-pinned page). apps/staging.yaml at stage-3 lines 23-25: automated, selfHeal: true, prune: true.

git show stage-3:deploy/k8s/lessons/retain-storageclass.yaml lines 8-11: name retain-local, provisioner rancher.io/local-path, reclaimPolicy Retain, volumeBindingMode WaitForFirstConsumer. Output shows standard with the same PROVISIONER and VOLUMEBINDINGMODE and marked (default); retain-local is not. Lesson now names both the name and default-class differences.

Line numbers and copy correct (line 28 adds storageClassName: retain-local; 41-45, 50-56 as stated). Round 2: lesson now says "The Pod writer names both claims as its volumes", which matches sed line 30 adding a Pod-level volume for kept; the container-mount wording is gone.

reclaim-policy.sh lines 9-12: custom-columns=CLAIM:.spec.claimRef.name,CLASS:.spec.storageClassName,RECLAIM:.spec.persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy,STATUS:.status.phase, then awk keeps the header and lines starting with data or kept.
Output block in the lesson matches outputs/stage-3/scripts/k8s/reclaim-policy.txt line for line: data/kept Bound before; only "kept    retain-local   Retain    Released" after both deletions.

Only source is the script's own comment (line 59). Kubernetes docs (Retain step 1: "The associated storage asset in external infrastructure still exists after the PV is deleted") support the general idea, but local-path behaviour is not in any allowed docs root; cluster run not permitted here. The lesson attributes it to the comment, which limits the damage.

kind docs: "The node is a container created by kind." and "Extra mounts can be used to pass through storage on the host to a kind node for persisting data". Round 2: §6 ("in kind, a folder on one node"), §9 line 5 ("in kind, a folder on one node, gone with the node or cluster") and q6 now state it only for kind.

PersistentVolumeClaimSpec: "storageClassName is the name of the StorageClass required by the claim." The spec has no reclaim-policy field (none listed in the PersistentVolumeClaimSpec table); persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy exists only in PersistentVolumeSpec.
persistentVolumeClaimRetentionPolicy whenDeleted: "Retain (default)"; "The default for policies is Retain, matching the StatefulSet behavior before this new feature."
Conditioned recommendation ("suits data you would rather clean up by hand than lose") with its cost stated; consistent with docs: Retain "allows for manual reclamation of the resource".
Definitional distinction (backup = separate copy elsewhere). The factual support it leans on (copy lost with node/cluster) is kind-specific and is handled under claim 14.
